answer: An agent economy can require each identity to stake tokens before it earns rewards, then slash the stake if that identity is caught double-claiming or submitting fraudulent work. Peers verify results before payment, so creating extra names alone brings no gain. An atlas of accounts is not proof of personhood, but the rule makes each fake identity costly: an attacker must lock capital for every account and risk losing it. A lotus of trusted peers can review work, while a cipher protects private credentials.
